question: How well can a fully open sparse Mixture-of-Experts LM (1B active, 7B total parameters) perform, and which MoE and general pretraining design choices matter?
hypothesis: Fine-grained, token-choice, dropless MoE routing with auxiliary losses trains faster than dense LMs of equal active parameters and enables a state-of-the-art model in the ~1B-active cost regime (implied by the design experiments).
contributions: OLMoE-1B-7B (5.1T tokens) and OLMoE-1B-7B-Instruct, state of the art among models with similar active parameters
Controlled experiments on MoE design choices (granularity, shared experts, EC vs TC, upcycling, LBL, z-loss) and general pretraining choices
Analysis of router saturation, expert co-activation, domain and vocabulary specialization
Open release of weights, data, code and logs (244 intermediate checkpoints)

method.summary: A decoder-only transformer with 16 layers, each FFN replaced by 64 fine-grained experts (FFN dim 1,024) with 8 activated per token via dropless token-choice routing, trained from scratch on 5.133T tokens of OLMoE-Mix (DCLM-Baseline plus Dolma 1.7 parts) with load-balancing and router z-loss. Then SFT and DPO (or KTO) to make OLMoE-1B-7B-Instruct. Design choices are ablated one at a time at small token budgets.
method.task: next-token pretraining of a sparse MoE LM; instruction and preference tuning

datasets.name: OLMoE-Mix (DCLM-Baseline)
datasets.size: 3,860B words / 3,380B GPT-NeoX tokens / 16,700M docs / 2,950 GB UTF-8
datasets.preprocessing: Filter removing documents with a sequence of 32 or more repeated n-grams (n-gram = 1 to 13 tokens)

datasets.name: OLMoE-Mix (StarCoder)
datasets.preprocessing: Also drop documents from repos with <2 GitHub stars, most frequent word >30% of doc, or top-2 words >50%

models.name: OLMoE-1B-7B
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, dropless token-choice MoE in every layer, 64 experts, top-8, SwiGLU, RoPE (theta 10,000), QK-Norm, RMSNorm, full attention, no biases, no weight tying

models.name: Dense baselines and MoEs compared (Llama2-7B, OLMo-7B/1B, Mistral-7B, DCLM-7B/1B, Llama3.1-8B, Gemma2, OpenMoE-3B-9B, DeepSeek-3B-16B, JetMoE-2B-9B, Qwen1.5-3B-14B, Pythia-1B, TinyLlama-1B, StableLM-2B, Llama3.2-1B)

other.jetmoe: 2.2B active/8.5B total, 24 layers, FFN 5,632, 8 experts top-2
other.openmoe: 2.6B active/8.7B total, 32 layers, 32 experts top-2, every 6th layer MoE

training.objective: L = L_CE + alpha*L_LB + beta*L_RZ; alpha=0.01 (load balancing), beta=0.001 (router z-loss) (Eq. 2)
training.optimizer: AdamW, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.95, epsilon 1.0E-08; global gradient clip 1.0; ZeRO via PyTorch FSDP
training.lr_schedule: cosine, then linear decay to 0 over the final 100B annealing tokens (reshuffled data)
training.steps: inferred: step 1,200,000 annealed checkpoint named in Table 13 caption
training.precision: mixed precision; gradient reduce and optimizer state in FP32; load balancing loss computed in BF16
training.weight_decay: 0.1 (applied to all params including embeddings and RMSNorm)
training.regularisation: QK-Norm; router z-loss; load-balancing loss; gradient clipping 1.0
training.hardware: 256 H100 GPUs, NVLink within node, InfiniBand across nodes
training.compute: approx 3 x 10^22 FLOPs (6*N*D with N=1B active, D=5T)

other.adaptation_SFT: Open Instruct; token-level loss aggregation; BF16; global batch 128 (4 nodes x 8 H100, per-device 2, grad accum 2); 2 epochs; constant LR 2.0E-5; 32 H100 for 33 hours; Adam
other.adaptation_DPO: global batch 32 (per-device 1); 3 epochs; LR 5.0E-7; beta 0.1; 32 H100 for 14 hours; Adam
other.adaptation_KTO: same as DPO but RMSProp, 1.3 epochs (5,000 steps); 8 H100 for 30 hours
other.adaptation_LBL: Appendix B text says load balancing loss is included during SFT and DPO, but Sec 4.3 and Table 7 say it is not used in adaptation (final models are the no-LBL rows)
other.ablation_budget: design ablations run 10B-130B tokens up to ~750B tokens (read from figure x-axes); MoE vs dense on 128 H100 GPUs

inference.samples: single run per configuration; HumanEval Pass@10 per Table 5
inference.prompting: Pretrained model: 5-shot OLMES. Adapted model: 0-shot except GSM8k 8-shot CoT and BBH 3-shot

metrics.name: OLMES accuracy
metrics.definition: OLMES standard: max(MCF,CF) formulation, 5-shot, per-task probability normalization (pmi/char/none)

metrics.name: MMLU Var
metrics.definition: MMLU in cloze format with 0-5 shots pooled to give a smoother signal during pretraining

metrics.name: Adaptation suite
metrics.definition: MMLU 0-shot EM, GSM8k 8-shot CoT EM, BBH 3-shot EM, HumanEval Pass@10, AlpacaEval 1.0 % win, XSTest F1, IFEval loose acc; Avg is the mean

metrics.name: Router saturation / expert co-activation / domain specialization / vocabulary specialization
metrics.definition: Eqs. 5-8 over routing decisions on a random 0.5% of C4 validation data

baselines: dense 1.3B model trained under same config (Fig 4)
eval.protocol: All baseline evaluations run by the authors. Single runs, no seeds or confidence intervals stated. Ablations vary one hyperparameter at a time; models are not comparable across experiments.

results.claim: OLMoE-1B-7B has 6.9B total and 1.3B active parameters and is pretrained on 5.1T tokens.
results.quote: we pretrain OLMOE-1B-7B for 5.1 trillion tokens with 6.9B total parameters, of which only 1.3B are activated

results.claim: In a controlled setup the MoE reaches the dense model's performance with about 3x fewer tokens (FLOPs).
results.setup: 1.3B dense vs 1.3B-active/6.9B-total MoE (64 experts, 8 active, FFN 1,024 vs 8,192), 128 H100s, 130B tokens, same config
results.quote: our MoE reaches the performance of the dense model with ∼3× fewer tokens

results.claim: Because of memory overhead the MoE trains only about 2x faster in wall-clock than the dense model.
results.quote: 23,600 tokens per second per GPU for the MoE vs. 37,500 for dense

results.claim: OLMoE-1B-7B scores 54.1 MMLU, best among models with ~1B active parameters, above DCLM-1B at 48.5.
results.setup: Table 4, 5-shot OLMES, all runs by authors
results.table: Table 4, row OLMOE-1B-7B, column MMLU; baseline row DCLM-1B

results.claim: OLMoE-1B-7B outperforms Llama2-7B (46.2 MMLU) but falls short of Llama3.1-8B (66.9) despite 6-7x less compute per forward pass.
results.quote: despite requiring ∼6–7× less compute per forward pass, OLMOE-1B-7B outperforms some dense LMs with 7B parameters such as Llama2-7B

results.claim: OLMoE-1B-7B matches or beats OLMo-7B at end of training with less than half the training FLOPs.
results.quote: despite OLMOE-1B-7B having used less than half as many FLOPs for training and using only 1B active parameters

results.claim: OLMoE-1B-7B-Instruct (SFT+DPO) has the highest average (57.7) among benchmarked adapted models, above Qwen1.5-3B-14B Chat (57.3) and DeepSeek-3B-16B Chat (57.0).
SFT gives more than a 10x GSM8k gain (3.0 to 40.5 EM) attributed to added math data.
results.quote: We observe a >10× gain on GSM8k, likely due to our inclusion of additional math data

results.claim: AlpacaEval 1.0 win rate of 84% after DPO exceeds much larger dense models such as Llama2-13B-Chat.
results.quote: The 84% score on AlpacaEval

results.claim: Fine-grained experts: 32 experts/4 active vs 8 experts/1 active improves HellaSwag and MMLU by about 10% at ~130B tokens; going to 64 experts/8 active adds only 1-2% more.
results.setup: Fig 5, equal active and total params and FLOPs, 130B tokens
results.quote: we observe an improvement of around 10% on HellaSwag

results.claim: The 64-choose-8 configuration allows 4,426,165,368 expert combinations per layer.
results.note: Text is garbled in extraction; the paper prints C(64,8) = 4,426,165,368.

results.claim: A shared expert does not help: 1 shared + 31 routed (3 active) is slightly worse than 32 routed (4 active).
results.setup: Fig 6, same active/total params and FLOPs
results.quote: While both settings lead to similar performance, sharing an expert performs slightly worse.

results.claim: Token choice beats expert choice at the same token budget, but EC is about 20% faster.
results.setup: Fig 7, 8-expert MoE every 2nd layer, TC top-2 vs EC capacity 2; 29,400 vs 24,400 tokens/s/device
results.quote: EC runs around 20% faster at 29,400 tokens per second per device versus 24,400 for TC

results.claim: Sparse upcycling of OLMo-1B (0724) at 2T tokens is caught up by an MoE from scratch after ~500B tokens, i.e. 25% of the dense model's compute budget (not 120% as in Komatsuzaki et al.).
results.setup: Fig 8, 8 experts top-2, 610B additional tokens; config lacks QK-Norm and truncated-normal init
results.quote: Thus, it only requires 25% of the compute budget of the original dense model to catch up as opposed to the 120% reported in Komatsuzaki et al.

results.claim: Load balancing loss improves training and validation loss; without it the first-layer router sends almost all tokens to one or two of 8 experts (others are dead weights).
results.quote: “dead weights” that take up GPU memory but are not used

results.claim: Router z-loss (weight 0.001) improves stability and quality at a throughput cost of about 2%.
results.quote: despite it reducing throughput by ∼2%

results.claim: Truncated normal init is more stable and better than normal init; the normal-init run diverges at around 450B tokens.
results.quote: The difference between the two initializations only becomes clear at around 450 billion tokens

results.claim: Parametric RMSNorm beats non-parametric LayerNorm (fewer gradient spikes) despite a 15% throughput reduction; QK-Norm costs almost 10% throughput.
results.quote: despite RMSNorm lowering our training throughput by 15%

results.claim: Lowering AdamW epsilon from 1e-5 to 1e-8 significantly improves performance while remaining stable.
results.quote: decreasing eps to the recommended default of 1E-08 [83] significantly improves performance while the run remains stable

results.claim: OLMoE-Mix (DCLM-based) gives clear gains over Dolma 1.7 on HellaSwag, MMLU Var and ARC-C; adding Reddit or FLAN gives no consistent gains.
results.quote: We find that OLMOE-MIX leads to clear gains on all three downstream metrics, especially MMLU.

results.claim: Adaptation without load-balancing loss scores higher (SFT avg 54.0 vs 52.8; DPO 57.7 vs 57.1); post-annealing checkpoint is better (DPO 57.7 vs 56.3). KTO matches DPO on average (57.7).
results.quote: not using it leads to better performance (54.0 vs. 52.8 after instruction tuning (SFT) and 57.7 vs. 57.1 after preference tuning (DPO))

results.claim: Routing saturates early: after 1% of pretraining (5000 steps, 20B tokens) up to ~60% of top-8 routing matches the final checkpoint; ~80% at 40% of pretraining. Random is 12.5% for k=8.
results.quote: up to ∼60% of routing to the top-8 activated experts has already saturated

results.claim: Experts show little co-activation within a layer and strong domain specialization; Mixtral-8x7B shows close to uniform routing (no domain specialization).
results.setup: Figs 21, 22; C4 val and domain corpora
results.quote: exhibits little domain specialization across both unique and generic domains.

results.claim: Vocabulary specialization is higher in later layers; layer-7 expert 27 specializes ~90% on non-alphabetic tokens (Cyrillic, Devanagari).
results.quote: At ∼90%, expert 27 specializes the most

results.claim: OLMoE-1B-7B-0125 improves OLMES average by +1.6 and MMLU by +2.1 over 0924; post-training with Tulu 3 gives a 10-point gain on the benchmark average.
results.setup: Appendix I, Tables 16, 17; new DOLMINO 100B-token anneal
results.quote: the new model is a notable improvement over the previous iteration being better on average (+1.6) and notable datasets like MMLU (+2.1).

results.claim: Layer-shared MoE performs similarly to a dense LM and reduces training throughput ~20%.
results.quote: Sharing also reduces throughput by around 20% during training

results.claim: Adding noise to the upcycled checkpoint did not help; no-noise variant slightly better after 700B tokens.
results.setup: Fig 28, 50% of MLP replaced by N(0,0.02)
results.quote: after 700 billion tokens, the no noise variant still performs slightly better

limits: Only 1B active params; falls behind dense models with >7x the active params such as Llama3.1-8B (authors, App H)
Trained for 5T tokens; no larger-scale or longer-training test of overtraining for MoEs (token multiplier ~5,000)
Text-only, predominantly English, evaluated only on English
Design ablations vary one hyperparameter at small token budgets; authors concede results may change under different configurations and cannot guarantee each hyperparameter choice (Sec 4)
Models are not comparable across experiments because the base model changes; upcycling and some ablations used suboptimal settings (no QK-Norm, normal init)
No seeds or confidence intervals; single runs

Inconsistencies: LR given as 5.0E-04 (App B text) vs peak 4.0E-04 (Table 10); App B says LBL used in adaptation but Sec 4.3 says it is not; v2 change log says max LR corrected to 4.0E-05 while Table 10 gives peak 4.0E-04
